section_1.title: The Familiar World: Euclidean Distance
section_1.content: Introduce the standard metric on real numbers. Visualize the number line where distance is |x - y|. Explain that a series converges if its partial sums get closer to a point in the standard sense.
section_1.example: A hopping frog on a number line; as it jumps smaller and smaller distances (1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8...), it lands closer to the point 1.

section_2.title: The 2-adic Perspective: Defining the Valuation
section_2.content: Introduce the 2-adic valuation v2(n), which counts the highest power of 2 dividing n. Define the 2-adic absolute value: |x|_2 = 2^(-v2(x)). Visual aid: Represent numbers by their binary trees—the deeper the '2' factor is, the 'smaller' the number.
section_2.example: Compare |8|_2 = 1/8 (very small) vs |7|_2 = 1 (not divisible by 2). This flips our intuition: powers of 2 are 'tiny'!

section_3.title: The Non-Archimedean Mystery
section_3.content: Explain the Ultrametric Inequality: |x + y|_2 ≤ max(|x|_2, |y|_2). This creates a 'no-carry' logic. Use a visual 'nested circle' diagram where points are contained in balls that either don't intersect or are fully contained within one another.
section_3.example: Two robots moving on a 2-adic grid; they don't move in a straight line, but jump between hierarchical clusters.

section_4.title: Infinite Sums: Convergence Reversal
section_4.content: Show that in the 2-adic metric, the series Σ 2^n converges to -1. Explain that for a series to converge in 2-adics, the terms must approach 0 in the 2-adic sense (meaning they must be divisible by increasingly higher powers of 2).
section_4.example: A digital accumulator device: 1 + 2 + 4 + 8... in the 2-adic world, this sum fills up the 'bits' to infinity, effectively completing the representation of the number -1.

section_5.title: Conclusion: A New Mathematical Reality
section_5.content: Summarize how changing the definition of 'distance' changes the convergence of infinite series. Emphasize that 2-adic analysis is foundational for modern number theory and cryptography.
section_5.example: A lens-shift effect: Viewing the same set of numbers through a standard magnifying glass vs. a 2-adic prism to reveal the hidden structure.
